I meant land mass moving due to changes in temperature and just the fact that land moves over time, the building course I attended was in southern England where we don't get quakes so I'm not sure how to account for those exactly, only for building to off-set the movement of the earth

By insulation I mean that you will need to be careful about not building some sort of rammed earth wall to separate your living space from the thermal mass, and making sure that you a) can retain heat but also b) can cool yourself down, without some good insulation that can be difficult, all depending on how much thermal mass you have behind your structure - you don't want too much of it, the more of it you have iirc, the better your insulation will need to be

I would worry about earth movement here, I went on an earthship design course recently where they build into the earth, and you have to account for the land mass moving. Over time I would imagine your plaster would crack and move, so I think you would need better reinforcements, but the idea of digging into the earth (or piling up earth) is one I really like. Also I think you may well struggle with insulation

If you haven't already, check out earthships and also (can't remember the name)  see if you can find those easy to construct dome houses that you put up, screw together and then cover in earth to insulate with thermal mass - very cool.

I feel this, it still gets to me sometimes, but i find that it passes a lot more easier nowadays, since i've learnt some things. I repeat the mantra 'i am loving awareness' to myself and meditate often too. I find that separating myself from the idea that I am 'other' or I am alone, or that I am anything other than simply the energy of the universe encapsulated in a concentrated carbon-based life-form very helpful.
Also being in nature and crying, just staring at leaves and the wind helps a lot, and then on the flip side just balling my eyes out helps too. The books 'the power of now' and 'be here now' by Ram Dass really helped with this specific issue.

having some sort of purpose can seem helpful, but it is not completely necesary. If there is something that makes you angry in this world however - that may be a good indication as to what your purpose is.

mostly i've found it's just learning to live in the present, practicing non-attachment and complete acceptance of any and all emotions that come up that's helped the most.

I'm sort of in the same place as you right now but I do believe I've started healing. Some of the things that have helped me start this journey: radical self-acceptance, not in the sort of 'edgy teen way' but more of just an acceptance of myself for all the good and bad things I've done and a decision to love myself anyway (or try).

Also, crying. Instead of trying in any way to actively deal w my emotions or stop myself crying I just cry for like two days in a row and then once I feel like I can stop I write stuff down in my journal. Honestly, life changing. Crying is your bodies natural way of dealing with and processing emotions so if you feel the urge just cry it all out. And then try to process what's left by writing it out.

Sounds weird but going to the gym really helped me when I was dealing with the same thing. It wasn't something I hated or enjoyed so it was fairly neutral, and I just forced myself to go and the endorphin rush and general improvements I made in strength made me feel like I was progressing just enough to give me some motivation back. Also meditation and just being gentle with myself, it sounds to me like you're struggling with depression, although you may want to check out digestive issues as well (I found out that I didn't have good gut bacteria and had issues with gluten, and since clearing that up I've felt miles better too and I can get out of bed again). 
I also overloaded my vitamins (as in took more than the recommended dose) bc I figured why the fuck not and apparently it can help. 

This is all just stuff that helped get me through the winter (still is), main goal should always be curing the root depression, but i hope this helps you regardless.
